verdict: Intel's revenue fell 4% to $13,674M and the core business made a $580M operating profit — but a $671M tax charge on just $338M of pre-tax income turned the quarter into a $333M total net loss.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted, attributable to Intel; non-GAAP EPS was $0.15

kpis.label: Data Center and AI
kpis.note: +9% YoY — the growth engine this quarter

segments.name: Data Center and AI
segments.note: Server CPUs and AI products for datacenters. Up 9% YoY.

segments.name: Intel Foundry
segments.note: Chip manufacturing for outside customers only (most Foundry revenue is internal and eliminated on consolidation).

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Mostly Mobileye, plus smaller businesses; down 48% YoY mainly because Altera was deconsolidated in Sep 2025.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Developing new CPUs, AI accelerators and process technology; down from $3,876M a year ago.

opex.name: Marketing, general and administrative
opex.note: Sales, marketing and back-office costs of $1,174M, partly offset by a $30M net restructuring credit — reversals on earlier restructuring actions were larger than new charges — for a net $1,144M. Down from $1,239M a year ago on the gross figure.

follow100Note: One line dominates the bottom line: tax took $4.91 of every $100 of revenue — more than the quarter's entire operating profit per $100 ($4.24).
otherDetail: Other expense of $242M net combines two lines: interest and other, net of -$145M and a $97M loss on equity investments, net. Tax was a $671M charge — a 198.5% effective rate on $338M of pre-tax income, as reported by Intel.
footerNote: Net loss attributable to Intel was $591M (EPS -$0.12); the $333M total net loss is after $258M of income attributable to non-controlling interests.

takeaways.title: Data center carried the quarter
takeaways.text: Data Center and AI revenue rose 9% to $4,737M, while client computing fell 7% to $8,193M. Total revenue fell 4% to $13,674M and gross margin eased to 36.1% from 39.2%.

takeaways.title: Tax turned a profit into a loss
takeaways.text: Intel made a $580M operating profit, but a $671M tax charge on $338M of pre-tax income (a 198.5% rate) produced a $333M total net loss. On Intel's non-GAAP basis, EPS was a $0.15 profit.

takeaways.title: Cash generation was strong
takeaways.text: Intel generated $4.3B of operating cash flow in the quarter, launched its first 18A products (Core Ultra Series 3), and completed the $5.0B sale of stock to Nvidia.

oneTimers: Tax: the $671M tax charge on just $338M of pre-tax income — a 198.5% effective rate, as reported — is what turned an operating profit into a net loss. Intel's non-GAAP tax rate was 12% and its non-GAAP EPS was a $0.15 profit.

sources.label: Form 10-K for the year ended Dec 27, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)
